sections.content:
24,865 people

were counted on the census as "travel agents" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Travel agents advise travellers upon travel arrangements, make bookings, and receive payment for travel arrangements made.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "travel agents" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 35 to 39 years. Of the whole working population 11.5% were aged 35 to 39 years. For people working as "travel agents", 13.7% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "travel agents" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "travel agents" included:

  • importers and exporters
  • restaurant and catering establishment managers and proprietors
  • chartered and certified accountants

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "travel agents" there were more women than men (76.1% compared with 23.9%).

This means "travel agents" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "leisure, travel and related personal service occupations".

Men made up 23.9% and women made up 76.1% of "travel agents"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "travel agents" included:

  • early education and childcare services proprietors
  • podiatrists
  • careers advisers and vocational guidance specialists

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "travel agents" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "travel agents" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "travel agents", 8.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (56.5% compared with 43.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (84.4%) than self-employed (15.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
